interpretations.scope: Nominal case, seed 17, frozen offline_reach_hold_v1 acceptance, frozen timing/tolerances and stable controller.gvs_normpc@7.0.0; current campaign feedback only.
interpretations.statement: Outcome 0 (execution 054cb6d5) is a fresh, valid, jointly accepted nominal point (F414, F430, F460, F454) that is strictly dominated by the retained incumbent on every sampled physical metric: terminal_error_m 0.003195 m (F415), holding_max_error_m 0.003323 m (F360) and holding_max_speed_m_s 0.013737 m/s (F350) versus the incumbent's recorded 0.002698 m, 0.002730 m and 0.012750 m/s. Outcome 1 (execution dfb3b398) is a valid_failure (F501, F461, F325) whose sole failing component is sampled holding speed 0.054581 m/s (F482, F405); it changes more than one path, so it is confounded and says nothing about the unchanged incumbent.
interpretations.uncertainty: Identity-based incumbent comparison is classified unavailable because configuration identities differ, so the comparison above is descriptive against recorded incumbent metrics; one execution per configuration; no causal attribution and no continuous-time guarantee.

interpretations.scope: Recorded campaign control-weight points at the retained structure; descriptive association only.
interpretations.statement: Sampled holding speed at the frozen structure is not monotone in the frozen control tip-speed weights: higher holding penalties recorded higher sampled holding speed, and the one control-weight change that lowered holding speed did so while enlarging terminal and holding position error. Control-only adaptation therefore currently yields only trade-offs or failures, which motivates an isolated structural probe at frozen weights.
interpretations.uncertainty: Single executions, confounded representation differences between initializer records, and only two weight values per axis executed; no monotonicity, causality or continuous-time claim is made.

plan.hypothesis: Under the frozen nominal case, seed 17, stable controller.gvs_nmpc@7.0.0 and frozen numerical settings, raising the far-segment bending section scale design/far_section_scale from the incumbent 0.95 to 1.00 and 1.05, with every other path (including both control tip-speed weights at 0.05) held at the incumbent, produces one fresh nominal complete closed-loop execution per point; if far-segment stiffening reduces residual tip motion, at least one point is jointly accepted (joint_reach_holding_passed, acceptance 'accepted') with sampled holding speed not larger than the incumbent's 0.012750 m/s and terminal/holding position error not larger than 0.002698 m / 0.002730 m, giving a componentwise non-dominated eligible candidate; otherwise both points characterise this axis as a trade-off or failure. No directional effect is assumed or guaranteed.
plan.rationale: Action: structure_search with search.family_explicit@1.0.0 on one untested continuous structural path, because the newest nominal seed17 feedback probed only the near-section axis (1.00 dominated pass, F415/F360/F350; 1.05 confounded holding-speed failure, F482/F405) and the control-only axes have given only a speed/position trade-off or failure. The incumbent is at the granted lower bound of both section scales, so a non-dominated point cannot come from reducing scale; the far-segment section scale is the directly analogous untested continuous axis. I change exactly one path per candidate (single-change, incumbent-relative) so each point is interpretable, hold robot, task, acceptance, controller implementation and all numerical settings fixed, and keep both control tip-speed weights frozen at 0.05/0.05 so there is zero control adaptation and all variation is structural. Each selected value set rebuilds the structure/workspace/warm states and runs one unchanged stable-v7 closed loop on the nominal case, seed 17; there is no hidden inner adaptation search and no extra control budget. Method rationale: the explicit method evaluates my own ordered points with null step; two levels on one bounded coordinate give only a minimal dose-response, not a mathematical optimization, and no categorical material choice is interpolated. Expected information: whether far-segment stiffening can lower sampled holding speed without worsening terminal or holding position error; a joint pass with non-worsening metrics would be an eligible candidate for retention review, whereas a dominated pass or holding-speed failure closes this axis and directs the remaining untested paths (segments/near length, segments/far length, material scenarios). Control adaptation allocation: none (weights fixed). Counterevidence: acceptance is six-sample with no continuous-time guarantee, identity-based comparison with the incumbent is unavailable, the far-section response is unmodelled, and local evidence cannot guarantee nonlinear reach, braking or perturbation robustness. Exit criteria: complete evaluation plus profile of both changed configurations, or first material/unknown failure, or budget/correction ceiling.
stopping_conditions: Both changed configurations reach complete evaluation and profile (target_changed_configurations=2).
Any material or unknown execution failure, fail-closed under stop_on_material_failure.
Insufficient complete reservation or cumulative request/correction ceiling.
Any candidate fresh nominal joint pass with componentwise non-worsening metrics ends search and triggers retention review.
weakening_observations: The single changed near-section 0.96 execution on the perturbed near_z_plus case failed holding speed at 0.0676 m/s (execution 8b8ce269); it is case-confounded and weakens any prior that raising a bending section scale lowers holding speed.

The fresh near_section_scale ~1.00 point (execution 054cb6d5) was jointly accepted but strictly worse than the incumbent on all three sampled metrics (F415 0.003195 m, F360 0.003323 m, F350 0.013737 m/s versus 0.002698 m, 0.002730 m, 0.012750 m/s), so a structural scale increase is at least as likely to worsen as to improve.
Sampled holding speed is not monotone in the frozen weights, so a frozen-weight structural probe may land on a non-monotone response.
The incumbent already sits at the granted lower bound 0.95 of both section scales, so no downward structural scale move is available to recover position error.

arguments.reasoning: The new bound feedback is the two nominal seed17 points of batch-acf51de37cc32112. Outcome 0 (054cb6d5) is a fresh nominal joint acceptance (F414 true, F430 'accepted', F460 true, F454 true) with terminal_error_m 0.003195 m (F415), holding_max_error_m 0.003323 m (F360) and holding_max_speed_m_s 0.013737 m/s (F350); all three are strictly worse than the retained incumbent's recorded 0.002698 m / 0.002730 m / 0.012750 m/s, so it is a dominated pass, not a promotion. Outcome 1 (dfb3b398) is a valid_failure (F501 false, F461 'valid_failure', F325 false) whose only failing component is sampled holding speed 0.054581 m/s (F482, F405), and it co-varies a near-section scale change with terminal weight 0.025, so it is not isolated and its failure does not describe the unchanged incumbent. Together with earlier control-axis evidence (a speed/position tradeoff at higher terminal weight, holding-speed failure at lower terminal weight) these results leave the control-only direction without any non-dominated point, and the incumbent already sits at the granted lower bound 0.95 of both section scales, so no downward structural scale move exists. The analogous untested continuous structural axis is design/far_section_scale. I therefore choose structure_search, not diagnosis (the retained prediction/plans/motion read has no bound numerical comparison here and cannot resolve a structural response) and not STOP (the structural region is still largely unmeasured and legal budget remains).
